newsitem.title: USA: Oroville, Calif., says to draw down on bond reserve.
newsitem.headline: Oroville, Calif., says to draw down on bond reserve.

text.p: Oroville, Calif., said on Friday the city would have to draw down on bond reserves in order to pay in September holders of two revenue bond issues.
The Oroville Public Financing Authority issued two series of revenue bonds in 1992 to fund street, lighting and sewer improvements, for a total of $3.64 million.

Delinquencies on property assessments supporting the bonds forced the city last March to draw on the bond reserve to pay bondholders. The reserve funds for the bonds were drawn upon on March 15 in the total amount of $68,017, the city said in a statement.
Oroville said it expected that the reserve funds for the revenue bonds would be drawn upon once again on September 15 for an additional $108,172 in order to fully pay investors.

After these reductions, the reserve funds will hold a total of $183,811. The authority said this amount should be sufficient, together with anticipated assessment collections, to pay debt service on the revenue bonds on March 15, 1997.
However, the city warned that there may be insufficient funds available to make full payment of debt service on the revenue bonds on September 15, 1997 if foreclosure efforts are not successful.
The city plans to foreclose on delinquent property owners and sell the properties to raise revenues to ensure bondholders are paid in full.

The revenue bonds were underwritten by First California Capital Markets Group Inc. First California has been the subject of a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation for its work on bond offerings by several other California localities.
